title: Rav Sama
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Menachot 42a relates that Ravina and Rav Sama were sitting before Rav Ashi. Rav Sama saw that the corner of Ravina’s cloak was frayed … he said to Ravina, “Does the Master not hold…?” He [Ravina] replied, “It was said of the time of making.” Rav Sama was embarrassed. Rav Ashi said to him: “Do not be distressed; one of them is like two of us” (and Ravina was from the Land of Israel — Rashi). Hyman strongly endorses the Gaon’s proposal in Isaac Halevy’s Dorot ha-Rishonim, part 2, that the reading should be Rav Abba and Rav Sama son of Rava, and he identifies this Rav Abba as indeed a native of the Land of Israel, as explained in his entry.
He is mentioned in Bava Metzia 10b after Ravina.

notes.text: Saved Davidson Menachot 42a describes the fraying cloak corner; saved Rashi there explains the hole/fringe distance and explicitly says Ravina was from the Land of Israel. Hyman nevertheless endorses replacing him with Rav Abba and identifying Sama as Rava’s son; that is his emendation, not the named edition’s text. The work abbreviation עדה״ד remains unidentified, so that bibliographical source question is held. The earlier note’s assertion of a tentative expansion does not establish one.

Five whole saved scalars were read and checked against raw SHA256, exact selectors and actual edition metadata: Davidson Menachot42a text8 (262 characters) and text9 (91), and Vilna Rashi42a text8/index0 (165), text8/index1 (70), text9/index2 (44). These are the selected whole scalars, not a claim to have read every scalar in either full folio array. The main text explicitly has untitled proper-name Ravina and full Rav Sama sitting before full Rav Ashi; it describes the frayed cloak corner and gives the timing reply. He [Ravina] replied is a disclosed conversational inference from the exchange, not a newly printed personal name in the second אמר ליה or an admitted identity edge. The source's first דר׳ אשי can locally be rendered full Rav Ashi because this exact scene spells רב אשי; its later full Rav Ashi is also literal. Every explicit full Rav Sama/Abba title remains; Ravina and Rava remain proper names without invented full Rav expansions. Rashi discusses the opening/fringe distance and two explanatory alternatives; the current corner-fraying wording is supported context, but no unsupplied measurements, knot law or second alternative is inserted into Hyman's abbreviated body. The source DOES THE MASTER NOT HOLD genuine question and the missing completion remain, followed by AT THE TIME OF MAKING, Sama's embarrassment and Ashi's DO NOT BE DISTRESSED. ONE OF THEM is like TWO OF US keeps its contrast and numbers. The selected Rashi explicitly says one of the sages of the Land of Israel and Ravina was from there; that is attributed Rashi context, not a new independently admitted birthplace or a harmonization with Hyman's replacement Abba. Hyman's VERY RIGHT/SHOULD READ endorsement of the Gaon, and Rav Abba REALLY WAS a native of Israel/SEE HIS ENTRY, retain their confident force as Hyman's emendation and identification, not the received Davidson or Rashi wording and not genealogy/chronology admission. Rav Sama SON OF Rava remains Hyman's proposed reading, not a new paternal binding. עדה״ד remains unexpanded and unidentified; part TWO/page474 is preserved without invented book metadata, edition or exact wording of that work. The old note's reference to a tentative expansion supplied no actual identification and is not retroactively fulfilled. The named42a comparisons are digital editions, not observed printed letters or correction history. The historical Fable PASS and prior editorial decisions remain archived model/root records, not an automatic current admission. All source, two historical/current English versions, original mixed note and current note, inherited source question, draft audit context, original Fable return and full proposal were read; they remain exact. The preceding notes record the earlier state of the research. In Hyman’s printed entry (vol. III, p. 965), the abbreviation is בעדה״ר and the page number is 474. The supplied Hebrew instead has בעדה״ד. The argument occurs at pp. 574–575 of Isaac Halevy’s Dorot ha-Rishonim, part 2 (Frankfurt, 1901). Halevy gives Rav Sama’s patronymic in parentheses and proposes that Rabbi Abba was replaced by Ravina in the text and in Rashi. Hyman endorses that proposal. The consulted Menachot 42a and Rashi name Ravina. Hyman’s printed Bava Metzia citation is 10a, but the consulted text has Rav Sama speaking after Ravina on 10b.
